slides.title: People in Society
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 4 English, Unit 6: People in Society. Unit 6 is about the people who keep a community working: the helpers, the leaders, and the newcomers. You will meet a caretaker, a carpenter, an engineer and a merchant, then governors, senators, lawyers and the military, and finally artists, photographers, messengers, refugees, immigrants, tenants and consumers. You will use the Present Simple to say what each person does, should and mustn't to give advice and rules, prepositions to say where people go, and the past tenses to retell what happened. By the end you will describe the helpers in your own town, just as Amal does in the story “The Community Parade”. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name and describe at least twenty jobs and roles that people play in society.
Explain what different workers and leaders do, using the Present Simple.
Give advice and state rules using should and mustn't.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name and describe at least twenty jobs and roles that people play in society. You will also explain what different workers and leaders do, using the Present Simple. You will also give advice and state rules using should and mustn't. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: caretaker, carpenter, labourer, engineer, merchant, governor. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Two Neighbours: A Refugee and an Immigrant
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The People of Our Town and Two Neighbours: A Refugee and an Immigrant. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Present Simple: describing everyday jobs

slides.narration: The first language focus is Present Simple: describing everyday jobs. We use the Present Simple for routines, facts, and things that happen again and again. It suits jobs perfectly, because most jobs repeat every day: “The caretaker cleans the school every morning.” Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Describe a Job. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
